events.text: Fire destroys most wooden elements; major reconstruction follows.

evidence.quote: The fire in the 1360s destroyed most of the wooden elements

events.text: Lead roof is replaced by a copper roof.

evidence.quote: was replaced by copper in 1474

events.text: Carta Marina shows a fire beacon on Neuwerk.

evidence.quote: The Carta Marina shows a fire beacon on Nuge uirk as early as 1539

events.text: Copper roof is replaced by a tiled roof.

evidence.quote: This was again replaced in 1558 by a tiled roof

events.text: Count Palatine Johann Rist resides at Neuwerk.

evidence.quote: In the 1600s Royal Protestant Imperial Count Palatine Johann Rist resided at Neuwerk

events.label: coal fire beacon
events.text: Open coal fire beacon is first mentioned in sources.

evidence.quote: other sources mention the open coal fire beacon not until 1644

events.label: coal supply
events.text: Beacon requires 1000 tons of Scottish coal yearly.

evidence.quote: This required 1000 tons of imported Scottish coal a year starting from 1761

events.label: lighthouse conversion
events.text: Tower is turned into a lighthouse.

evidence.quote: The tower was only turned into a lighthouse on December 20 , 1814
used as lighthouse ( 1814–2014 )

events.label: triangulation point
events.text: Tower marks northernmost point of Gauss's Hannover triangulation.

evidence.quote: The tower marked the most northern measuring point for the triangulation of the Kingdom of Hannover by Carl Friedrich Gauss in July 1825

events.label: lamp fuel
events.text: Lamp starts burning colza oil and kerosene.

evidence.quote: burned on colza oil and kerosene starting 1870

events.label: Fresnel lens
events.text: Fresnel lens is installed with a five-wick kerosene lamp.

evidence.quote: A fresnel lens of measuring a focal length of 700 mm was installed 1892

events.label: lamp upgrade
events.text: Lamp is improved again.

evidence.quote: The lamp was again improved in 1908

events.label: small lighthouse demolished

evidence.quote: The small lighthouse was torn down in 1909

events.label: copper for military
events.text: Copper roof material is used for military purposes.

evidence.quote: The copper was then used for military purposes in 1916

events.label: electrification

events.label: halogen lamp
events.text: Electric lamp is replaced by a halogen lamp.

events.text: Lighthouse is decommissioned and handed to Hamburg Port Authority.

evidence.quote: decommissioned on January 1 , 2014 and turned over to the Hamburg Port Authority

events.label: LED lamp
events.text: Lamp is replaced by LED.

events.label: lighthouse shut down
events.text: Lighthouse is officially shut down after almost 200 years.

evidence.quote: On February 10 , 2014 it was officially shut down after almost 200 years in operation

undated_mentions: Tower is the oldest building in Hamburg and the oldest secular building on the German coast
Original purpose: host troops to defend ships on the Elbe against pirates
Tower served as refuge for islanders during storm surges and shipwreck survivors
Original roof was made of lead
Scharhörn reef was marked by beacons and bearing aids before the lighthouse conversion
Nord-Bake still shows the beacon form
Original open coal beacon was replaced by the small lighthouse after the great lighthouse started operating
Kerosene lamp kept in place with no emergency power supply
Light could be seen from Heligoland; reach of about 30 km
Lighthouse was operated by Wasser- und Schifffahrtsamt Cuxhaven
Original light characteristic was switched to a steady white lamp with reach of about 3 nautical miles
Lighthouse continues as a private light under Hamburg authority
Electricity was needed to shut the light down quickly during World War II
Tower is used as viewpoint, guesthouse and restaurant
Attic was home to the bird warden of Verein Jordsand for many years
Sinstorf church is older; part of Hamburg since the Greater Hamburg Act of 1937 (refers to the church, not the tower)
